mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevation of RESIDENTIAL mobility above +14 percent across all four observed weeks shows households have locked into a stay-at-home routine that does not decay within a month, so discretionary trips that feed retail-and-recreation footfall stay suppressed and RETAIL_REC drifts no higher than its current trough.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL printed 14.3, 15.4, 14.3 and 15.9 in the four weeks to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages above its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above +13 percent throughout the same window.

mechanism_narrative: Outdoor activity is the marginal driver of discretionary footfall: when the PARKS weekly mean crosses below -40 percent, ambient pedestrian flow collapses and the residual retail-and-recreation demand generated by park-adjacent trips disappears, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean crosses below -40 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS printed -45.6 at t-2w and -40.0 at t-0w, below the -40 threshold
failure_condition: In weeks where the PARKS weekly mean sits below -40, RETAIL_REC rises over the following 14 days in more than half of observed cases.

mechanism_narrative: Commuting is a joint product of workplace and transit activity, so TRANSIT and WORKPLACES falling together signals that the entire work-trip chain, including the lunchtime and after-work retail it supports, is shut down; the tandem decline keeps RETAIL_REC pinned at its depressed level over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both print below -45 percent in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT -54.4 and WORKPLACES -47.0 at t-0w, both deeply negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remaining below -45 percent.

mechanism_narrative: The joint signature of TRANSIT below -50 and RESIDENTIAL above +14 is the fingerprint of a hard containment regime; while that signature persists, non-essential retail capacity stays closed and RETAIL_REC cannot recover, so it remains at or below its current 28-day average.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -50 percent while RESIDENTIAL stays above +14 percent
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT averaged -53.6 and RESIDENTIAL averaged +15.0 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT remains below -50 and RESIDENTIAL remains above +14.

mechanism_narrative: Households are reallocating a fixed trip budget toward essentials: GROCERY_PHARM holds a roughly 30-point advantage over RETAIL_REC, and as long as that gap persists the substitution channel keeps discretionary retail visits crowded out, holding RETAIL_REC flat to lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC exceeds +25 points in the latest week
evidence_refs: fact:at t-0w GROCERY_PHARM -26.7 versus RETAIL_REC -59.6, a 32.9-point gap
failure_condition: The GROCERY_PHARM-minus-RETAIL_REC gap narrows below 20 points and RETAIL_REC nonetheless falls further over the following 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The late-November holiday shopping build-up begins regardless of containment and pulls RETAIL_REC off its trough, because gift and grocery-adjacent purchasing shifts online-to-storefront and into the essential-retail perimeter that remains open; the seasonal lift dominates the restriction drag over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC has been range-bound between -56.7 and -60.1 for four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages below its last-28-day mean, rejecting the claim that holiday-season demand lifts it despite containment.

mechanism_narrative: De-escalation from the hardest containment tier restores a first wave of discretionary trips: as soon as TRANSIT posts a week-on-week gain of more than 3 points while RESIDENTIAL ticks down, RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks because reopening re-permits non-essential storefront access.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 3 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL falls versus the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved -52.3, -54.9, -52.9, -54.4 and RESIDENTIAL moved 14.3, 15.4, 14.3, 15.9, showing week-to-week oscillation rather than monotone tightening
failure_condition: TRANSIT gains more than 3 points week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL declines, yet RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is not above its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Behavioural fatigue shows up as a flattening RESIDENTIAL series: the four-week change is only +1.6 points even though containment deepened, meaning households are no longer cutting trips further; with WORKPLACES also flat at about -47, the erosion pressure on RETAIL_REC stalls within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL four-week change is smaller than +2 points while WORKPLACES stays within 1 point of -47
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL moved from 14.3 at t-3w to 15.9 at t-0w, a +1.6 point change; WORKPLACES stayed between -46.4 and -47.9
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises by more than 2 points within the next week and RETAIL_REC falls over the following 7 days, contradicting the fatigue-stabilisation claim.
